_purpose: Every calibrated number and every exception in one place, each with a written reason. A reasonless entry fails its guard.

rulesRegistry._retiredNote: An id retired here is never reused (G-10). Retiring leaves a visible gap rather than a silent renumbering, so anyone holding an older registry sees a deliberate absence.
rulesRegistry._adapterNote: The law of the split: the adapter holds identity, layout, commands and pointers — never a rule body. Checked with the same parser that reads the registry, so the two cannot disagree about what a rule definition is.

evidence._threshold_rationale: Enough to cover a wrap-up cycle and a baseline comparison without the directory becoming unbrowsable. Not a durability guarantee: evidence/runs/ is gitignored operational output, not knowledge.
evidence._enforcementEnvironmentRationale: Stamped on every run header. Boundaries here are enforced by the permission engine and hooks, not by the operating system — the Bash sandbox needs macOS, Linux or WSL2 (G-07). An evaluation produced under a different regime is not comparable to one produced here, and TASK 9 exports this harness to machines that differ, so the regime travels with the trace rather than being assumed.
evidence._traceEventsRationale: The event vocabulary, as data. check-trace derives what it accepts from this list rather than carrying its own copy, so adding an event to the writer without declaring it here fails loudly instead of validating as 'unknown' forever.
evidence._traceHeaderReasonsRationale: Same shape as traceEvents directly above it: the vocabulary lives in config so a writer emitting an undeclared run.header reason fails loudly instead of validating as unknown forever. 'startup' and 'delegated' are the two values the real corpus emits today (TASK 12 slice 4's decision record: 118 headers across 101 files, every one reporting one or the other). 'observed' is declared now but not yet emitted — it is reserved for TASK 12 slice 5, which will make the writer record the real permission_mode once the runtime exposes it, distinguishing an actually-observed posture from an assumed one. Declaring it here means slice 5 does not have to touch this list, and the two slices stay independent.
evidence._maxRequestLossRateRationale: Measured, not chosen: the repository's own trace carried 63 orphan tool.result events — a tool.requested the runtime never delivered, not a writer defect — over 3,754 tool.result events recorded across the corpus, 1.68%. 0.02 leaves headroom without hand-picking a number to make today's corpus pass. This is a RATCHET, the same shape as T-03's mutation floor: the rate may not rise, and the only correct response to a rise is finding the lost writes, never a bigger number. retainRuns above prunes old run directories, so the denominator drifts with the corpus exactly as the mutation score's denominator drifts with the surface it measures.
evidence._recordedHookEventsRationale: Which runtime events must be wired to record-event.mjs. check-trace asserts settings.json carries every one — a hook nobody registered fires zero times and reports nothing, which is INC-08 exactly.
evidence._opaqueFieldsRationale: These three, and only these three, are opaque API-generated random tokens, never authored text — a 4-character banned term appeared inside a tool_use_id during a researcher run and failed the gate on a true string match carrying zero confidentiality risk (INC-15's family; TASK 18). Excluded BY FIELD NAME, read from this list, never by a "looks like an id" heuristic, which would widen itself silently over time and could come to exclude a field that actually carries publishable content. Every other field on an event — including target.file_path, and including one nobody has invented yet — is still scanned exactly as before, and a line that fails to parse is still scanned too: the exclusion never grows itself. Same family as check-terms.mjs's own terms.opaqueFields (integrity, for lockfile hashes) but a separate list, because the two guards blank different fields for different reasons.

exclusions._purpose: Paths excluded from repo-wide scans. This list is the ONLY roster in the guard suite, and it is an exclusion list rather than an inclusion list on purpose (INC-07): forgetting to add a path here makes a scan noisier, never blinder.

paths.reason: version control internals, not authored content
third-party code, not ours to audit
the confidentiality mapping itself; scanning it would report every banned term as a hit
machine-written trace, gitignored, already redacted at write time

generated intermediate (TASK 8): src/*.dc.html with public OFL webfonts expanded to base64 data: URIs. Gitignored, regenerated on demand by build.mjs — the base64 is third-party font binary, not authored content, and trips the scanner the same way any opaque blob does
cached raw woff2 files build.mjs downloads from Fontsource's CDN. Gitignored, third-party, not ours to audit

third-party code, not ours to audit. The repo-root node_modules entry does not cover it: isExcluded matches a prefix from the repository root, so a nested tree needs its own entry (found 2026-08-24, before the first npm install rather than after it slowed every gate run)
the build artifact. Gitignored, regenerated by astro build, and a copy of content already scanned at its source
Astro's generated type and content-store cache. Gitignored, machine-written, not authored content
Stryker's sandbox (TASK 15): a mutated copy of the repository, regenerated by every run and gitignored. Scanning it would report every banned term twice and every mutant as authored content
Stryker's HTML mutation report (TASK 15). Machine-written, gitignored, and a rendering of source already scanned at its origin

the smoke tier's per-failure output (TASK 41): traces, screenshots and error-context dumps Playwright writes when a test fails. Machine-written, gitignored, regenerated by every run, and a copy of markup already scanned at its source
the smoke tier's HTML reporter output (TASK 41). Same category as the entry above and as reports/: a rendering of results, not authored content

contextBudget._threshold_rationale: No documented total budget exists — the vendor guidance is <200 lines PER instruction file, not for the sum. 320 is a judgment call: it is above the ~261 lines projected once step 4 rewrites CLAUDE.md thin, leaving roughly 60 lines of growth before it complains, and below the current total so the gate names the outstanding work instead of staying quietly green. Lines are a coarse proxy for context cost, chosen because they are stable and trivially checkable.

fields.name: status
fields.reason: the delegation gate (H-05) refuses to launch a write-capable role while a spec is draft. Remove this field and the gate cannot tell.

fields.name: version
fields.reason: drift detection compares it against approved_version.

fields.name: approved_version
fields.reason: the gate compares it to version. Remove it and every spec silently reads as approved.

fields.name: tdd
fields.reason: T-01 keys TDD on work-item type AND surface, so a feature item touching the content pipeline requires it while the same item touching only presentation does not. Without this field the spec cannot record which it is, and the implementer has to guess.

fields.name: tdd_rationale
fields.reason: a spec that opts out of TDD must say why. P-03: an inapplicable dimension is declared out loud, because silence reads as coverage.

fields.name: reproduces
fields.reason: a bugfix with no bug-reproducing failing test is not done (T-01). Without the field the requirement has nowhere to land and quietly stops being met.

fields.name: behaviors
fields.reason: behaviors are the atomic unit a spec exists to carry; without them a spec is a summary.

fields.name: descends_from
fields.reason: every eval case names its incident. A case with no origin is one nobody can justify keeping.

fields.name: required_evidence
fields.reason: an eval scored on the agent report measures the model, not the harness (A16).

fields.name: forbidden_behavior
fields.reason: the bypass attempt is usually the real test (P-14).

templates._note: Each required field is a COUPLING between a template and a guard that reads it. Dropping one disarms the guard silently — INC-08 shape. Every entry carries a reason; a reasonless entry fails the check.

boundaries._note: One policy, two vectors. settings.json deny rules cover the file tools; the PreToolUse guard covers the shell, which deny patterns cannot reach reliably. Both are needed: neither alone closes the boundary.

delegation._purpose: H-05's inputs. The gate reads write-capability off the role's own tools list and the approval state off the spec file; these entries say where those artifacts live and which tools are known to be read-only.
delegation._readOnlyToolsRationale: An ALLOWLIST of read-only tools, never a roster of write tools. The direction is the whole point (P-13, P-16): a tool the runtime ships next month is unknown here, so the gate treats it as write-capable and gets stricter. A write-tool roster would silently wave the new tool through, which is INC-07's shape.
delegation._specRequiredForRationale: The work-item types whose approved artifact is a spec file, per the Work Item model in TASKS.md. Every other type approves something else — an ADR, a content file, a diff — so gating them on a spec would deny legitimate work, and a guard that blocks real work is a guard someone turns off.

_roleWriteScopesRationale: A20/A21. ONE role is enforced, not four, and the asymmetry is the decision: harness-evaluator's conclusions are only worth something if it cannot edit what it scores. implementer and test-engineer keep procedural scopes — named in the brief, checked by the auditor — because enforcing them has no incident behind it yet. The trigger for adding them is two roles writing concurrently. An allowlist, unlike `boundaries`, which is a denylist: a role named here may write NOWHERE except the listed prefixes, and a role not named here is unaffected.

procedures._doneBlockRationale: The date the done-block convention landed in progress/README.md, at blueprint step 3. Logs written before it are not retroactively required to carry one: demanding it would force either inventing evidence for finished work — which C-01 forbids for numbers and the same logic forbids here — or an exclusion roster of filenames, which is INC-07's shape. A dated threshold with a written reason is neither: a NEW log cannot slip through it, which is the property that matters.
procedures._iterationSplitRationale: TASK 72: the date the `iteration_split` dimension becomes required alongside `iterations`, so K1 stops reporting a bare count nobody can act on. Third use of the same dated-threshold mechanism as doneBlockRequiredFrom and iterationsRequiredFrom, reused rather than duplicated. Required only where `iterations` reads `passed` -- a not_applicable count has no cycles to attribute. The bucket vocabulary is NOT configured here: it is derived from the work-item procedure's own step headings and the register's own type table, because a hardcoded bucket list is the shape INC-07 fired on.
procedures._iterationsRationale: SPEC-TASK-13 (TASK 13, Capture K1): the date the `iterations` dimension becomes a required part of the done block, so K1 (implement->verify cycles until the human accepts done) stops being unmeasurable for a procedure reason. Same mechanism and precedent as doneBlockRequiredFrom, reused rather than duplicated: a dated threshold with a written reason, so a NEW log cannot slip through it and a log predating the cutoff is not retroactively demanded to carry a dimension nobody told it to when it was written.

docs._excludeRationale: The findings document records a resolution that is superseded once architecture.md is frozen. It cites paths as they were proposed during the review, several of which were then decided against — checking it would demand files a decision deliberately did not create.

ignore.reason: the registry's PRE-MOVE location, named in the KEEP/MODIFY matrix precisely to say that it moved to .claude/rules/. The reference is correct because the file is absent.
TASK 32's Deliverable. Same class. Note the sibling .github/workflows/harness.yml DOES exist and is checked normally, so this entry hides nothing that is currently checkable.

TASK 19's Deliverable. Blocked on the author copying three real LinkedIn recommendations into resources/, which H-02 puts outside every agent's reach — so the file cannot be created here to satisfy the check.
TASK 19's Deliverable, Spanish half. Same blocker as its English pair; C-09 requires both locales in the same change, so they arrive together or not at all.

docs._ignoreRationale: An EXCLUSION list, so forgetting an entry makes the check noisier and never blinder (INC-07). Every entry carries a reason, a reasonless one fails, and an entry whose target starts resolving is reported as stale so the list shrinks on its own.
docs._forwardLookingPathsNote: Every entry after the first is one class: a `TODO` work item's Deliverable naming a file that does not exist YET. Stated without a count on purpose - the previous wording said 'four of these five' and had already rotted twice by the time anyone read it, which is the same defect the site's own copy rule forbids: no visible string says how many of a growing thing there are. check-docs cannot distinguish 'planned' from 'stale' — both are a path that does not resolve — and teaching it to would mean parsing the register's entry shape inside a rung-2 guard, which is a work item with its own red-path battery (T-04), not a side edit. Until then this list carries them, and the self-staling property is what keeps that honest: every entry announces itself the moment its target appears. Added 2026-08-23, when the local-first re-cut found check-docs had been red behind check-trace's short-circuit for an unknown number of runs — three of these predate that session's edits. The ADR-007 entry was removed on 2026-08-23 the moment TASK 33 created its target — the self-staling property doing exactly what it was built to do, reported by check-docs rather than remembered.

filledLater.reason: empty until the case is run. A fresh case with no verdict is the normal state, not a defect.
written with the outcome, and only meaningful beside one.
set only when a case stops being useful. Present-and-empty is the healthy state (G-10).
required only when proof is none, which validateCases enforces conditionally. Demanding it everywhere would fail every case that HAS a proof.

evals._filledLaterRationale: The required-field set is DERIVED from EC-TEMPLATE.yaml minus these four, rather than listed. An inclusion list has to be updated by whoever adds a template field - the one moment they are thinking about something else - and a forgotten entry makes the guard blinder. Subtracting makes a forgotten entry merely noisier, which is the direction every exclusion list in this repository points (P-13).

excluded.reason: dev-not-equal-prod: seven element-level defects survived two visual reviews against a dev build. Its remedy is the visual-QA rigor checklist, deferred in architecture.md section M until the site has screens worth diffing. There is nothing to execute against today, and a case asserting on a build that does not exist would be documentation wearing a case filename. Returns with the first rendered page.

INC-16: a completed notification read as a finished report, and the orchestrator writing into a run that was still alive. Its control is P-18, at rung 3 — the orchestrator reads the run's run.footer before treating the run as done. There is nothing to remove and re-run: G-06 already records that reading the footer's ABSENCE is rung 4 and that nothing checks it, so no guard can be neutered to make this case go red, and a case that passes because the orchestrator behaved well measures the model rather than the harness (A16). Returns the moment footer-absence has a reader: a case can then plant a footerless run directory and assert it is reported as not having terminated normally.

evals._excludedRationale: An incident with no case is normally a hole in the regression net. These are the ones where the hole is a recorded decision instead - each names why no executable form exists and what brings it back. A reasonless entry fails the check, and an entry whose incident no longer exists is reported as stale, the same rule the docs ignore-list follows.

content._universalRationale: The five keys every content file in the repository actually carries. C-14 originally named thirteen as if they applied to everything, which described no file: the eight pages carry five, the case studies carry more. A rule no file satisfies is a rule that gets disbelieved, and one disbelieved rule discredits the registry.
content._byTypeRationale: Required keys are keyed on the declared type, and an UNKNOWN type is a finding rather than a pass - it is either a typo or a content shape nobody has specified the keys for, and both need a human (P-13). Note outcome is NOT required: mobile-banking-platform carries none in either locale, and resources/ is read-only input, so demanding it would fail the gate on frozen content that cannot be edited. The `ui` entry is the chrome file: its nine required keys are GROUPS, one per template, and check-content asserts only that each group is present - parseFrontmatter is a key scanner rather than a YAML parser, deliberately. Leaf-by-leaf validation belongs to the collection schema at build time, so each level claims exactly what it covers (G-11).

noFrontmatter.reason: a GitHub profile README is rendered by GitHub, which shows frontmatter as literal text. It is English-only by decision (TASK 4) and carries no locale suffix, so it claims no pair either.
the intake questionnaire used to gather the author facts. It is an input to content, never published content, so it has no slug, no locale and no route.

content._singleLocaleRationale: Empty, and that is the healthy state: every locale-suffixed file today has its counterpart. An entry here would exempt a page from C-09, which is a hard rule, so each one would need a reason strong enough to survive review.

site._purpose: The site tree's shape, as ADR-008 decided it. check-site derives every assertion from the files on disk, so directory seven is checked rather than waved through (P-13).
site._coreNote: Framework-free by design: it is the surface node:test runs and Stryker mutates (30-testing.md, ADR-006). Importing Astro or reaching into site/src would take it out of node:test's reach, which is the only reason it sits outside src/.
site._gatewayNote: The sole caller of getCollection (S-02). Everything downstream receives props, so a locale-join defect has one place to live. Declared as a SET because the gateway is not one folder by nature: Astro requires the collection definition at src/content.config.ts and requires it to import astro:content, so that file is part of the content-access layer by construction. Naming the set declares where the boundary runs; it is not a roster of components.
site._tokenStylesheetRationale: S-05. THE declaration site for every colour, breakpoint and type step. The guard reads this file to learn which --* names exist and then requires every other stylesheet and component to name one instead of writing a literal - so a twelfth token costs no edit here and none in the guard (P-13). Declared as a PATH rather than derived, because 'the one stylesheet' is a decision somebody made, not a property of the tree: two files full of custom properties are indistinguishable from disk, and picking the larger one would be a heuristic that silently relocates the boundary. The canvas repeats its token block in all eleven .dc.html artboards, which is correct for independent mockups and is precisely what this stops from being carried across.
site._humanReadableAttributesRationale: S-01. Attributes whose value a person READS - a screen reader speaks aria-label and alt, a browser shows title and placeholder - so a literal in one is a visible string declared outside resources/**, exactly like a text node. Four rather than every attribute: class, id, href, data-* and the rest carry structure, and scanning them would fire on every class name in the site. The text-node half needs no config at all; it is derived from the markup. Known and accepted gap: an attribute added to HTML next year is not covered until it is added here, which is the one roster-shaped thing in this check - the alternative, a heuristic for 'looks like prose', widens itself silently and would fire on href values.
site._routeDeclarationSitesRationale: Where a path-shaped literal naming a REAL content slug is allowed to appear. Empty, and that is the healthy state: the route set is derived from the collection, so no source file should need to spell one out. Declared as a SET rather than left implicit for the same reason `gateway` is - the day one legitimately needs an exception, it is written here with a reason instead of the guard being edited. The slug side is NOT here: check-site derives it from the filenames under the content roots, so a sixth case study is covered with no edit (P-13). What this catches is a page hardcoding `/case-studies/<a real slug>` instead of asking the collection.
site._pendingRoutesRationale: TASK 41. A slug whose route the collection already derives but which no page module serves yet. The smoke tier asserts 200 over (derived routes MINUS these) and asserts that every slug named here still 404s — so the list is SELF-STALING: the day a page item routes one, the second assertion fails and the entry has to be removed. That second half is the whole reason this is not a skip list. Written as SLUGS rather than routes because a slug covers both locales by construction, so a locale added later needs no edit here (P-13). Every entry carries a reason naming the item that will route it, and a reasonless entry fails the check — the same convention docs.ignore follows, and for the same reason: an exclusion that cannot explain itself becomes permanent. This list is expected to reach EMPTY, which is the healthy end state, not a defect.
site._threshold_rationale: The author's convention, stated 2026-08-24 and recorded as theirs: at seven files a directory is split into context-named subfolders. No published style guide was found supporting a numeric cap and the search was not exhaustive (ADR-008, sub-decision 5) - so this is calibrated by judgment, not by a citation. Its known failure mode is a split that invents categories to absorb overflow, which is why S-03 also requires the subdivision to name a context.
site._packageRootThresholdRationale: S-03's SECOND calibration, and it is not the first one raised. The ordinary cap governs directories somebody organised, and its remedy is a split by context. The root of a package is not one of those: npm fixes package.json and package-lock.json there, and a tool that resolves its config from the project root fixes that too — checked against each tool rather than assumed (2026-08-27): astro.config.mjs and tsconfig.json are read from the project root by astro, astro check and the editor, while vitest and playwright do accept --config but resolve testDir relative to the config file, so moving them displaces paths for no structural gain. Their members therefore share an external requirement rather than a context, and the remedy the rule asks for is unavailable to them. 10 is derived rather than plucked: 6 at site/ today plus the arrivals that can actually be named — wrangler.jsonc (TASK 32), .npmrc, README.md, .gitignore. At 11 the answer is NOT a higher number; it is a file that did not have to sit at a package root. Derived from disk, never a roster: any directory holding package.json gets this calibration, including the repository root and a package nobody has created yet (P-13).
site._exclusionsRationale: Generated or third-party trees. Counting them toward the cap would fail every directory forever and say nothing about the code anyone wrote. `screenshots` is the smoke tier's image deliverable: one PNG per route per width per theme, so it passes the cap the moment the site has more than one route and says nothing about anyone's code. Gitignoring it was NOT enough on its own — this guard walks the real tree, not git's index, which is how it fired the first time the suite ran against the full route set. `test-results` joined it on 2026-08-27: the smoke tier's per-failure output: Playwright writes a directory per failing test holding trace.zip, error-context.md and screenshots. Machine-written, gitignored, regenerated by every run. It was already excluded from the term scanner and NOT from this walk — an asymmetry found on 2026-08-27, which is why it went unnoticed: the directory is empty on a green run, so the cap would first have fired on a RED one, at the worst possible moment. Same class as screenshots directly above it.
site._commentRecordIdRationale: S-08. The id shapes this repository actually mints: ADR/INC/EC/EVAL/SPEC records, work items, and the six rule surfaces of the registry. A PATTERN rather than a list of ids, so a rule written next month is caught without editing this. The sibling half of the reference set is not here at all - check-site derives it from the repository's own top-level entries, so a new directory needs no edit either (P-13).
site._styleExtensionsRationale: Read for their CONTENT, like sources, but for a different reason: the token assertion has to read the stylesheet to derive the sanctioned colour and breakpoint set, and a file the walker hands over empty makes that guard deny (G-13) rather than evaluate - which is what it did the first time it ran. Kept separate from sourceExtensions rather than folded into it, because that list is scoped by a stated property - only these can carry an import - and widening it to make an unrelated check work would leave three import checks scanning files the rationale says they should not.
site._sourceExtensionsRationale: Only these can carry an import. Every other file still counts toward the cap - the rule is about how many files a directory holds, not how many of them are code.

terms._opaqueFieldsRationale: Generated values whose content is a digest, not authored text. A sha512 integrity hash is base64, so every short character sequence is reachable by chance and a short banned term appears in one eventually - two did in site/package-lock.json on 2026-08-24. Excluded BY FIELD NAME, never by a looks-opaque heuristic, which would widen itself silently over time. Everything else on the same line, including package names and resolved URLs, is scanned exactly as before. Same family as INC-15, whose fix for the trace is TASK 18.
terms._termFlagsRationale: TASK 45: a short banned term collided forever with an unrelated public npm package name (site/package-lock.json), the sibling defect to opaqueFields but on the TERM side rather than the field side. The author's fix is PER-TERM word-boundary opt-in, never a global switch - a global switch would trade this false positive for a class of false negatives in compound identifiers, which is exactly where an internal system name shows up. The syntax lives in private/banned-terms.txt, which this guard cannot read (H-04), so it is documented here instead: a line wrapped `\b <term> \b` (both markers required, term trimmed between them) opts that one term into word-boundary matching; every other term keeps substring matching unchanged. A line carrying only one of the two markers is malformed and fails the run naming its line number (G-13) rather than being read as a literal. Known limit, recorded rather than fixed: the colliding package name is `<term><digit>`, and \b does not exist between a letter and a digit, so the flag clears it. If a future package were `<term>-something` instead, \b would match at the hyphen and the false positive would return - the flag is kept equal to the regex primitive on purpose, because a per-term human decision needs to be predictable, not clever.
